title: Sweden's digital life expands and contracts at once: AI adoption rises while people seek detox, social boundaries, and safer public-service access
source_unit: Internet Foundation Sweden, Swedes and the Internet 2026 annual internet-use study
geography: Sweden; residents surveyed about internet use, AI, digital public services, social media, mobile etiquette, and digital detox

observations.period: 2026; AI use, search substitution, and verification

denominator.unit: respondents in Study 1 of the Novus randomly recruited Swedish panel; major share of report data

ai_service_use.unit: percent of Swedes using AI services in 2026

google_ai_overview_use.unit: percent reporting use of Google's AI overviews

any_ai_use.unit: percent using either AI services or Google's AI overviews

reduced_google_use.unit: percent saying they Google less often than one year earlier

ai_answer_verification.unit: percent of AI users who usually double-check whether an AI answer is correct

ai_adoption_mechanism.value: AI is moving from a distinct tool into ordinary search and service routines, while verification remains a user-side repair behavior

observations.method: Internet Foundation annual study using several sub-studies; most data came from Study 1, collected mainly in January 2026 through the Novus randomly recruited Sweden panel, with a 59 percent participation rate and weighting to Statistics Sweden on gender, age, education, and geography.
observations.uncertainty: The study is a weighted survey of reported use and perceptions, not passive device measurement, verified search logs, or a causal evaluation of AI on work, learning, or information quality; question bases vary across sub-studies.
observations.subgroup: Swedish residents aged 16 or older for core population estimates, with age, gender, work, study, and internet-user breakdowns in selected modules.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI use may include light or incidental exposure through search interfaces and does not establish delegation, purchase, productivity, trust, or durable substitution away from search.

observations.period: 2026; digital mailbox adoption and age-conditioned usability

denominator.unit: Study 1 respondents, with item-specific bases for digital-mailbox users and age groups

digital_mailbox_use.unit: percent of Swedes using a digital mailbox in 2026

older_users_find_mailbox_harder.unit: percent of digital-mailbox users aged 76 or older who report that the service makes things harder

internet_nonuse.unit: percent of the population aged 16 or older not using the internet

digital_service_conversion.value: High digital-service adoption can coexist with age-specific friction, notification uncertainty, fragmented inboxes, and fear of missing a bill or official message

observations.method: Weighted Internet Foundation survey estimates with qualitative open-text responses about why digital mailboxes help or hinder; digital-mailbox usability estimates use the relevant user and age subgroup bases.
observations.uncertainty: Reported difficulty is not a measured missed-payment rate, administrative error, or causal effect of digital mailbox design; the study does not link a respondent to actual notices, bills, or remedy outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Swedish digital-mailbox users, especially users aged 76 or older and older women.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some older users may prefer paper for familiarity or overview even when digital services function technically; perceived difficulty does not imply universal exclusion or failed delivery.

observations.period: 2026; passive scrolling, digital detox, and mobile social norms

denominator.unit: Study 1 respondents with item-specific bases for scrolling, detox, and relationship questions

passive_scrolling_too_long.unit: percent saying they get stuck passive-scrolling on the phone for too long

feel_worse_from_scrolling.unit: percent saying passive scrolling makes them feel worse or more than 40 percent as reported in the release

completed_digital_detox.unit: percent who have completed a digital detox

interested_in_detox.unit: approximately percent interested in taking a break from digital life

detox_benefit.unit: approximately percent of people who took a digital pause reporting mainly benefits

mobile_social_deprioritization.unit: percent feeling deprioritized when someone they are with looks at their phone instead of them

digital_rebalancing_mechanism.value: Digital adoption is accompanied by emerging norms that treat attention, presence, sleep, and social reciprocity as scarce resources worth protecting

observations.method: Internet Foundation survey questions on passive scrolling, digital-detox behavior, perceived effects, and mobile etiquette, supplemented by open-ended responses; the items are self-reported and cross-sectional.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates do not measure screen-time logs, clinical wellbeing, actual sleep, relationship quality, or whether a detox persists; the release uses rounded language for some figures and different item bases may apply.
observations.subgroup: Swedish internet users and mobile users, with selected gender, age, relationship, and young-adult comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported interest in detox may be a cultural ideal or temporary response rather than durable behavior; scrolling can be entertainment or social contact as well as unwanted time loss, and phone use may coexist with in-person connection.

related_sources.claim: English report navigation and summaries for internet use, AI, social media, digital detox, and mobile etiquette.
Official 2026 summary with study design, sample, weighting, headline estimates, and chapter-level caveats.
Internet Foundation release provides the September 28 publication date and headline AI, digital-mailbox, scrolling, detox, and mobile-etiquette findings.

boundary: This record adds a Sweden-specific cultural and digital-life layer connecting AI diffusion, search substitution, verification, digital public-service usability, passive attention, detox, and mobile social norms. It does not establish actual AI performance, passive behavioral logs, clinical effects, service failure, household welfare, or causal cultural change.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Internet Foundation press release, 2026 report page, English navigation, and official summary PDF were reviewed for fieldwork, sample, weighting, AI and search measures, digital-mailbox use and age differences, passive scrolling, detox, mobile etiquette, and subgroup boundaries.
